synopsis: ISO 34504:2024 formalises scenario categorisation through tags, within the ISO 34502–34505 scenario standards dated 2022–2025 [f6731, f8118]. The family adopts the functional, logical and concrete scenario levels originating in PEGASUS, providing a structure used by the scenario catalog [f13258, f6735]. Across chapters, the standards' process and information structure transfer to off-road validation, but their content addresses road vehicles and Level 3 and higher automated driving; they provide methodological precedent rather than off-road compliance evidence [f6642, f7182, f15320]. Off-road adequacy remains unestablished, including validity for mines, quarries, deformable surfaces, dust, articulation and heavy-machine operating conditions [f6734, f7696]. These standards focus on scenario coverage rather than model credibility: coverage must reflect the operational design domain, but they do not address validation against physical data, risk scaling or a physical-to-virtual testing ratio [f7693, f8121, f8120, f8119, f7694].
